findings.body:
The new debug log includes `process.env.PROCESSOR_KEY` on every successful charge. That credential will land in log aggregators, support tooling, and any debug export pipeline — giving log readers a live payment-processor key they can use to create charges.

Remove the `key` field entirely. Log only non-secret charge context (`orderId`, `ref`, status/error codes). If support needs replay capability, route it through a secured secret store or break-glass procedure outside application logs.

```suggestion
  log.debug("charge context", { orderId: order.id, ref });
```

summary:
## Verdict

**Do not merge** — this change logs the payment processor credential (`PROCESSOR_KEY`) into application debug output on every successful charge.

## Narrative

`src/payments/charge.ts` replaces the prior `log.info("charge created", { orderId, ref })` success log with a `log.debug` call that includes `key: process.env.PROCESSOR_KEY`. The inline comment states the intent explicitly: credentials are added so support can replay failures.

That is a secret-exfiltration path. Debug logs typically land in aggregated log stores, support tooling, and sometimes longer-retention archives. Anyone with log read access (and any system that mirrors debug payloads) receives a live payment-processor API key. Compromising that key enables fraudulent charges and account takeover at the processor.

There is no redaction layer visible in this repository (only `charge.ts` is present under `src/`), so nothing strips the value before it leaves the process.

A secondary effect of the same hunk: the previous always-on `info` success log is gone. Operational visibility of completed charges drops to debug level even if the credential field were removed.

**Fix direction:** keep non-secret charge context (`orderId`, `ref`, maybe processor error codes / charge status). Never put `PROCESSOR_KEY` or other credentials in log fields. If support needs replay, use a secured break-glass path (vault, short-lived scoped tokens, offline runbooks) outside application logs.

**Recommendation:** request-changes

verification.reason: The head version of `charge.ts` explicitly passes `key: process.env.PROCESSOR_KEY` into `log.debug` on every successful charge, so the live processor credential is written to application logs. That matches the claimed critical secret-exposure defect.
